Coordinating with all treatment program staff and providing the day to day operational needs of the facility and its patients. The Certified Behavioral Health Technician is responsible for assisting, monitoring, and reporting of the condition of the facility and patients to ensure safe and orderly operations. The BHT is involved with overseeing and conducting certain intake procedures, including but not limited to obtaining data when a patient arrives to the facility, conducting searches and rounds, ensuring the safety of a patient during their treatment stay, and assisting the treatment teams with the overseeing of patients’ throughout their daily schedules within the facilities policies and procedures and in accordance with the standards of the State and Federal Regulations. Depending on an individual's safe driving record, some BHT’s may be involved with transportation and complying with vehicle and road/patient safety measures.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

● Assist with the supervision of patients; in their daily activities.

● Ensure that the patient’s follow the clinical schedule, and communicate any issues to the treatment team.

● Transport clients (when applicable) as needed (Must have valid Driver's license)

● Assist with preparing and maintaining rooms and common areas.

● Fosters a supportive environment for clients that follows ethical treatment.

● Reports to work per their assigned schedule and maintains acceptable overall attendance.

● Promotes a favorable/positive work atmosphere that is based on a team mentality.

● Completes all required training, and attends in-services and educational training as necessary and as assigned.

● Maintains flexibility and adaptability to expected and unexpected changes in the work environment.

 Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) - School & Home-Based, Adolescent Client
Miami Beach, FL | 30 Hours/Week | Immediate Start
My Time 2 Launch
Position: Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)
Location: Miami Beach, FL (school and in-home sessions)
Schedule: 30 hours per week. Most hours are during the school day, Monday-Friday, with additional after-school sessions in the home.
Start Date: Immediate
Pay: Based on experience
Reports To: Supervising BCBA
ABOUT MY TIME 2 LAUNCH
My Time 2 Launch is a neurodiversity-affirming ABA organization serving families in Florida, Georgia, and Michigan. Our clinical work is grounded in the Empowerment Model™, our strengths-based, dignity-preserving approach to Applied Behavior Analysis. We don't try to make people less themselves. We help them build the skills, confidence, and independence to live the lives they choose.
ABOUT THIS ROLE
We're looking for an experienced, emotionally attuned RBT to support a bright, academically capable high school student. This teen needs a steady, trusted presence to build social connections, stay organized and on track academically, and navigate the demands of the school day with confidence.
Most of your hours will be at school, supporting the student in class and during unstructured times. The rest will be at home after school, supporting routines, planning, and generalizing skills across settings.
This role requires more than technical skill. The right person is discreet, warm and patient. They understand teenagers, respect their autonomy, and know how to build rapport with someone who is smart, perceptive, and deserves to be treated as a partner in their own growth. Sensitivity to adolescent emotional wellbeing is essential.
HOW WE WORK: THE EMPOWERMENT MODEL™
 • Strengths first: We build on what the student already does well and what matters to them.
• Collaboration and assent: With a teen client, goals are pursued with the student, not done to them. Their voice shapes the work.
• Dignity-preserving practice: No restrictive or aversive procedures, ever. We protect privacy, independence, and self-respect, especially in front of peers.
• Built-in generalization: Skills are practiced across school, home, and real-world settings so they last.
• Family partnership: Caregivers are central members of the team.
• Data-driven, SMART goals: Clear, measurable progress guided by BCBA supervision.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
At School
 • Implement the student's individualized treatment plan during the school day under BCBA direction.

 A Day in the Life of a Lead Registered Behavior Technician
As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky.  • Delivers ABA sessions with an assigned caseload under BCBA direction.
• Models procedures and gives in-the-field feedback to newer RBTs.
• Covers sessions when teammates are out and supports high-need cases.
• Helps with new-hire shadowing, treatment-integrity checks, and team trainings.
• Shares front-line observations with BCBAs and the Clinical Director.
• Completes accurate data and session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.
 What Do You Bring to the Role?
 • Certification: Current RBT certification in good standing.
• Experience: Ten or more years of direct ABA experience for $27/hour; five or more for the lower end.
• Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.
• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.

 • Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.
 Physical Requirements
 This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

 A Day in the Life of a Lead Registered Behavior Technician
As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky. You model procedures for newer technicians, cover sessions when a teammate is out, and give your BCBA a front-line read on how each case is really going.
Every month you help shadow new hires, support treatment-integrity checks, and share what you see with our Clinical Director so quality stays high across the team. You love teaching as much as you love therapy, and you take pride in watching the RBTs you mentor grow into confident clinicians.
What Would You Be Doing?
 • Delivers ABA sessions with an assigned caseload under BCBA direction.
• Models procedures and gives in-the-field feedback to newer RBTs.
• Covers sessions when teammates are out and supports high-need cases.
• Helps with new-hire shadowing, treatment-integrity checks, and team trainings.
• Shares front-line observations with BCBAs and the Clinical Director.
• Completes accurate data and session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.
 What Do You Bring to the Role?
 • Certification: Current RBT certification in good standing.
• Experience: Three or more years of direct ABA experience.
• Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.
• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.
 Are you the person other technicians ask for help? Do you give feedback in a way that builds people up? Are your data and session notes always clean and on time? Can you stay calm and lead when a session gets hard? If so, you might just be perfect for this Lead RBT position!
RBT Success Profile
 • Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.
 Physical Requirements
 This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.

D & M Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach. From our office in Pembroke Pines, our bilingual team delivers family-centered ABA at home, at school, and in the community, and coaches caregivers so progress continues between sessions.

 A Day in the Life of a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT)
As a Registered Behavior Technician, you play an essential role in helping our clients reach their goals. You work one-on-one with children at home, at school, and in the community, delivering kid-centered ABA therapy through games, play, and everyday routines. You follow the treatment plan your BCBA designed, collect data in real time on ABA Matrix, and write a clear session note before you head to your next family. Because we build your caseload around your availability and your neighborhood, your schedule works for you.
You are never on your own. Your BCBA visits your sessions every month to coach you in the moment, answer your questions, and celebrate the wins with you. Each day brings new challenges and new breakthroughs, like a first word, a calm transition, or a caregiver who thanks you by name, and you find real fulfillment in knowing your work changes a child’s life.

 • Implements individualized treatment plans under the direction of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA).
• Teaches communication, social, play, and daily living skills through play-based and naturalistic ABA.

• Responds to challenging behavior using the strategies in the behavior plan.
• Checks in and out of every session at the point of care.
• Communicates professionally with caregivers, BCBAs, and the treatment team.
• Participates in monthly supervision and ongoing training.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.

• Technology: A tablet or laptop for session notes.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Experience: Six months of ABA experience is preferred.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.
 Experience with children with autism is a plus, but multiple factors will be taken into consideration. Are you patient, dependable, and playful? Are you organized and attentive to detail? Do you communicate well with families? Do you work well both independently and as part of a team? If so, you might just be perfect for this position in ABA therapy!
RBT Success Profile
 • Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.

 D & M’s mission is to help children with autism and their families build the skills, confidence, and daily routines to thrive at home, at school, and in the community.
D & M Behavioral Solutions of Tamarac, FL is looking to hire a part-time or full-time Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) on the BCBA track. Are you comparing RBT offers? Did you know an extra dollar an hour means nothing if you pay thousands for supervision? If so, please read on!
Join us, get paid as an RBT, and earn your BCBA fieldwork hours with free supervision from our BCBAs.
Why Work at D & M Behavioral Solutions?
 • Competitive Compensation: $19 - $24 per hour, based on your experience, education, and certifications, paid biweekly by direct deposit.
• Flexible Scheduling: Flexible shifts built around your availability and classes. We build your caseload around your availability and neighborhood.
• Health and Wellness: Our PreventivePay wellness program gives you 24/7 virtual urgent care, unlimited virtual doctor visits, and ongoing virtual primary care, with no waiting rooms.
• Mental Health Support: Confidential counseling with licensed mental health counselors, plus unlimited wellness support groups: yoga, sleep coaching, emotional resilience, whole-body wellness coaching, therapeutic art, grief and loss, managing chronic pain, quitting nicotine, a men’s group, and parenting support for moms.
• Real Savings: Free acute medications and up to 80% off other prescriptions at 70,000+ pharmacies, and up to 60% off dental care with 263,000+ dentists, where each family member picks their own dentist.
• Tuition Discount: Through our partnership with Purdue University Global, you and your immediate family (spouse or partner, children, parents, and siblings) save 14% on any graduate program and 20% on any undergraduate program, in fields like psychology and ABA, health sciences, nursing, business, education, human services, and information technology.
• Purdue Global Students: D & M is a Purdue University Global partner site, so Purdue Global ABA students can complete their supervised BCBA fieldwork hours with us.
• Free Fieldwork Supervision: Free BACB fieldwork supervision from D & M BCBAs (many future analysts pay out of pocket for this).
• Mileage: Reimbursed between client locations at the current IRS rate.
• Impactful Work: Help a child say a first word, make a friend, or get through the day with more independence.
 A Day in the Life of a Student Analyst
As a Student Analyst, you work as an RBT with your own families while you train to become a BCBA. You deliver ABA sessions, collect data on ABA Matrix, and start thinking like an analyst: why this program, why this prompt, and what the data are telling you.
Your D & M BCBA supervisor meets with you every month and assigns fieldwork activities that count toward your BCBA hours, like graphing data, drafting a program update, observing an assessment, or helping with caregiver training. Your hours are logged in the BACB Fieldwork Tracker, your schedule works around your classes, and when you pass your exam, a BCaBA or BCBA role at D & M is waiting for you.
What Would You Be Doing?
 • Delivers ABA sessions as an RBT with an assigned caseload.
• Completes BCBA-assigned fieldwork activities (graphing, program updates, assessment observation, caregiver training support).
• Meets with a D & M BCBA supervisor every month and logs hours in the BACB Fieldwork Tracker.
• Collects accurate data and completes session notes in ABA Matrix within 24 hours.
• Communicates professionally with caregivers and the treatment team.
• Maintains client confidentiality and follows D & M policies and the RBT Ethics Code.
 What Do You Bring to the Role?
 • Certification: Current RBT certification (or the ability to certify within 180 days).
• Education: Enrolled in, or accepted to, a master’s program with a BACB verified course sequence.
• Transportation: Valid Florida driver license, reliable car, and auto insurance.
• Background: Ability to pass a Florida Level 2 background screening.
• Commitment: Commitment to a consistent weekly schedule.
• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.
• Positive Attitude: Patience, reliability, and strong communication with families and teammates.
 Are you curious about why behavior happens? Do you love learning and asking questions? Can you balance classes, fieldwork, and client sessions? Are you ready to be coached and to grow? If so, you might just be perfect for our Student Analyst program!
RBT Success Profile
 • Functional and Technical ABA Skills: Baseline mastery of discrete trial training, prompt fading, reinforcement, and data collection.
• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.
• Seeking Help and Receiving Feedback: Recognizing your limits, asking your supervisor for guidance early, and accepting feedback constructively.
• Dealing Behaviorally with Stress: Identifying personal stressors and using self-management to maintain your stamina.
• Composure: Staying calm and objective during challenging behavior or crisis situations.
• Business Etiquette and Professionalism: Punctuality, professional appearance, and proper communication in homes and schools.
• Approachability and Listening: Putting clients, caregivers, and colleagues at ease while actively hearing their concerns.
• Customer Focus and Caregiver Rapport: Communicating with parents with empathy and without overwhelming technical jargon.
• Patience: Keeping the right pace during slow skill acquisition and staying tolerant under pressure.
• Time Management and Preparedness: Organizing session materials in advance and managing session time efficiently.
• Think Function: Viewing client and caregiver behavior through an environmental, function-based lens.
• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.
 Physical Requirements
 This role involves working in homes, schools, and community settings, occasionally lifting or moving up to 30 lbs., sitting on the floor, bending, kneeling, and engaging in active play for extended periods. Travel between client locations is required.
Who Are We?
D & M Behavioral Solutions is a South Florida ABA therapy provider serving children and families across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach.  We are currently seeking a qualified, dedicated, and compassionate Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) to provide in-home, school, and community-based Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) services. You will be a critical part of our team, helping children, youth, and young adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder or other developmental disabilities build skills and reduce challenging behaviors.
